name: Cory Booker
role: U.S. Senator from New Jersey (2013-present); Mayor of Newark (2006-2013); 2020 presidential candidate
summary: Booker is a mainstream progressive Democrat whose record centres on criminal justice reform (First Step Act, marijuana legalization, death penalty abolition), Medicare for All, baby bonds, a $15 minimum wage, and a reparations commission. He has a pragmatic, bipartisan streak (advanced nuclear bills, charter schools, support for Israel and NATO) and favours unity over confrontation. In 2025 he gave a 25-hour floor speech against the Trump administration, and in 2026 he led an Iran war powers resolution.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Cosponsored Sanders's Medicare for All bill in September 2017 and said in the 2019 debates that health care is a right and Medicare for All is the best way to cover everyone.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Backs a $15 federal minimum wage (2017 airport-worker remarks) and said in the November 2019 debate the minimum wage must rise to a living wage of $15.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Said in November 2019 that the estate tax should rise and capital gains be taxed as ordinary income, though he rejected Warren's wealth tax; in 2025 he denounced tax cuts for the wealthiest.

unions-good.rationale: Said in October 2019 he stood with striking workers because unions are under attack and that he would work to spread union strength, including sectoral bargaining.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Called for tighter antitrust enforcement and tech regulation in the 2019 debates and co-introduced the Algorithmic Accountability Act (2019); he also said regulation can slow some tech sectors.

cut-welfare.rationale: In the 2025 floor speech he opposed cuts to Medicaid and called government programs a lifeline created by the people, not a slur; Medicaid is the programme addressed, not all welfare.

state-harmful.rationale: In 2025 said government programmes are something the people created as a lifeline, and he has pursued new federal programmes throughout his Senate career.

limit-guns.rationale: Cosponsored an assault weapons ban and the Background Check Expansion Act and called for national gun licensing in the 2019 debates, while saying he defends law-abiding owners.

empower-police-military.rationale: Mixed: as Newark mayor he laid off police officers in 2010 and later called for more police in all neighborhoods; he also co-wrote the 2020 policing accountability bill.

rehabilitation.rationale: Led the bipartisan First Step Act, which expands job training and early-release programmes, and said in 2019 he believes in redemption and that locking people up has failed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Called New Jersey's civil unions discriminatory, cosponsored the Respect for Marriage Act (2014) and voted for it in 2022.

abortion-legal.rationale: Said in October 2019 he would fight to codify Roe, repeal the Hyde amendment and create an Office of Reproductive Freedom; votes against abortion restrictions are recorded.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Sponsors the bill to create a commission on reparation proposals (S. 40) and advocates baby bonds to close the racial wealth gap.

free-trade.rationale: Opposed fast-track authority for the TPP (2015) and USMCA until stronger labor and environmental protections; in 2019 said trade deals must put workers at the centre.

nation-first.rationale: In September 2019 said Trump's America First amounts to America alone and that U.S. strength is magnified by standing with allies.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: In 2013 said he opposed Syria intervention, then backed limited action with clear objectives and congressional involvement, and in 2017 criticised a strike without a plan or authorization.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Said in 2019 climate must be the issue and lens for every other, backed a Green New Deal-style ten-year mobilization, and sponsored the Climate Stewardship Act.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Said in 2016 that carbon-neutral power requires advanced nuclear energy and backed a bill for faster NRC licensing and more reactor research; again backed next-generation nuclear in 2019.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Said in November 2019 that the estate tax should be raised; his baby bonds plan was to be paid for by estate tax changes (not independently verified here).

basic-income.rationale: In October 2019 he said raising the minimum wage to $15 would do more for workers than a $1,000 monthly universal basic income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In 2025 he condemned trade wars against allies and warned tariffs would raise prices; in 2019 he criticised Trump's tariffs on allies while also saying China cheats.

political-violence-never.rationale: In May 2026 said political opponents should not be enemies or accept political violence from any side and that people now wrongly think violence is acceptable (reported paraphrase).

military-superiority.rationale: In 2013 said he wants the strongest military in the world; has also opposed weapons the military does not want.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said in 2019 voters want equality in opportunity as well as in wealth; he favours baby bonds but did not endorse equal outcomes as such.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Said in September 2019 that Democrats cannot sacrifice progress on the altar of purity and pointed to Newark school results as evidence.

taxation-theft.rationale: Repeatedly calls for corporations and the rich to pay their fair share and defends tax-funded programmes, which treats taxation as legitimate.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: His campaign site called him a strong advocate for Israel and said Israel's right to exist as a secure Jewish state is non-negotiable; his April 2026 vote against arms sales concerned the Iran war.

school-vouchers.rationale: Told the Washington Post in September 2019 that vouchers hurt educational equity, reversing earlier support; he had backed D.C.'s voucher programme months earlier, so the record is mixed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: In the 2025 speech he read Protect Our Care's argument that Medicaid work requirements only add red tape for working families. The point concerns Medicaid, a narrower case than welfare generally.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: In 2019 he named combating racial segregation and past redlining as parts of his education agenda.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: In 2019 he proposed banning fracking and new oil leases on public land and backed a Green New Deal-style mobilization.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Backs far wider government roles, including Medicare for All and Medicaid expansion, and objected in 2025 to treating government programmes as a slur.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said in 2019 that everyone has worth and dignity and that women are people; his record includes ENDA, the Respect for Marriage Act and the Equality Act.

separated-powers.rationale: Said in 2019 the president was refusing the checks and balances he owes Congress, and co-introduced a bill to protect the special counsel from removal.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Called child poverty a moral obscenity in the 2019 debates and in 2025 spoke at length for Medicaid and safety-net recipients against tax cuts for the wealthy.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: In the 2025 speech he asked where colleagues were when international students were taken from streets without due process.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Criticised Trump in 2019 and 2025 for abandoning allies and undermining alliances, saying U.S. strength grows when it stands with allies.

death-penalty.rationale: Said "we should abolish the death penalty in America" at federal and state level and is a cosponsor of the Federal Death Penalty Prohibition Act.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Said in 2019 that in presidential elections the person with the most votes should be president, while saying the next election must be won under current rules.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Supports a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict even with settlements, which implies territorial compromise; no direct statement on ceding land.

collective-defense.rationale: Voted yea on the 2022 ratification of Finland and Sweden joining NATO and against Rand Paul's amendment saying Article 5 does not override Congress's war power.

ban-cartels.rationale: Called for stronger antitrust enforcement against corporate consolidation in the 2019 debates and introduced a bill with a moratorium on agricultural consolidation.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Said in 2019 trade deals must put workers at the centre and American values lead on trade and workers' rights; opposed USMCA until environmental and job protections were stronger.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Supports affirmative action, saying both race and class should be considered and citing Grutter v. Bollinger.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Voted for the Employment Non-Discrimination Act (2013), cosponsored the Equality Act and led the Justice for Victims of Lynching Act.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Called in 2019 for starting impeachment proceedings because the president acted against the Constitution, and in January 2021 called for the 25th Amendment or removal.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Vegan; has proposed legislation to ban new factory farms and close existing large ones by 2040 and said in 2019 that factory farming harms the environment and independent farmers.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: In August 2017 he announced a bill to remove Confederate monuments and memorials from the Capitol.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: In 2025 he defended Social Security as an earned promise funded by workers' paychecks and, in 2019, proposed raising the payroll tax cap to fund it.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said in 2019 corporate power is trying to influence Washington through Citizens United and refused to take corporate PAC money; named cosponsor on campaign-finance amendments.

job-guarantee.rationale: Has spoken in favour of a federal jobs guarantee and proposed a pilot programme rather than a full guarantee.

socialized-care.rationale: Cosponsored the Child Care for Working Families Act (2019), which subsidises child care; this does not make all care a public service.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Original cosponsor of the Equality Act (2019); called Trump's transgender military ban deplorable and said in 2019 it would end it on day one.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Signed on to the Be HEARD Act (April 2019), which ends mandatory arbitration and pre-employment nondisclosure agreements for harassment claims.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Became a cosponsor in October 2019 of the Senate resolution recognising the Armenian genocide, which passed by unanimous consent.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Supports cap-and-trade or a carbon tax to curb emissions per summaries; his stated position has varied on a carbon tax specifically.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Said in October 2019 he would fight to spread union strength and ensure sectoral bargaining so that unions from auto workers to fast-food workers can raise conditions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Supports expanding the Earned Income Tax Credit (2014, 2019) and proposed an EITC-based anti-poverty plan costing about $134 billion a year (January 2019), per a dated compilation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: A 2019 dated summary lists his support for loan forgiveness and for government not profiting from student debt; no recent primary statement found.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

voter-id.rationale: In 2026 said election rules should always have proof of citizenship, but opposed the SAVE Act as voter suppression.

women-suffrage.rationale: Listed suffragettes among the heroes he admires in his 2025 floor speech.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Said at the September 2019 debate that systemic racism is eroding the nation from health care to criminal justice.

notes: Views changed: vouchers (supported for years, then in September 2019 said they hurt equity, though he backed D.C.'s program that year); Medicare for All (open to single-payer in 2017, then backed it, later described himself as a pragmatist); Israel arms sales (opposed blocking them in 2024-25, voted to block certain sales in April 2026 tied to the Iran war); filibuster (defended in 2019, called for reform from 2021). Many statements are null because he has not spoken to them; Marijuana Justice Act covers cannabis only, not all drugs. The 25-hour speech in the Congressional Record is mostly health care, Medicaid, tax cuts and institutions.
